findings.failing_input: Pagination cap-warning false positive: when Meta returns a `paging.next` cursor on page 50 AND the cursor URL is valid, the warning fires. But there is no test for the case where page 50 has `data` but NO `next` cursor → does the loop exit cleanly without firing the warning?
findings.expected: Warning fires only when results were truncated (next cursor still present after 50 pages).
findings.actual: Looking at line 375 `if (safety >= 50 && url)` — if page 50 returned no next cursor, `url = body.paging?.next ?? null` sets url to null, then safety++ makes safety=50, loop exits, predicate `safety >= 50 && url` is false (url is null), warning skipped. Correct! However, the loop body increments safety AFTER processing page 50, meaning the cap is checked before page 50 — wait, re-reading: `while (url && safety < 50)` means we process pages 1..50 (safety goes 0,1,...,49 when entering, 50 when exiting). Correct.
findings.fix_sketch: n/a — code is correct after re-reading. Removing this finding.
findings.regression_test_idea: Test that 50 pages exactly with no nextPageToken on page 50 does NOT emit the warning.

findings.file_line: meta.ts:336 (URL construction with token in query string)
findings.failing_input: fetchMetaAdSetInsights / fetchMetaAdInsights / fetchMetaSpendForDayLight / fetchMetaBudgets all embed the Meta access token in the URL query string.
findings.expected: Per the file docstring, Meta API does NOT accept Bearer header so query-string is mandated. Documented and accepted.
findings.actual: Documented as T-05.6-04-I2 mitigation: token rides in URL. Server-side logs may leak the token if Vercel logs full URLs. Inngest logs the URL via console.error / step.run failures. The token would appear in any error string thrown by HTTP failures (line 345 `... failed (${res.status}): ${body}` — but the URL itself is not echoed in the error message — good). However, fetch() instrumentation libraries (OpenTelemetry, Vercel Analytics) WILL capture full URLs including query strings.
findings.fix_sketch: Document explicitly: no observability layer should be enabled that captures URL params. Add a runtime-config check or use `URL` API to strip search params before logging in error paths.
findings.regression_test_idea: Test that thrown error message does NOT contain the access token value.

findings.failing_input: fetchMetaSpendForDay calls fetchMetaAdSetInsights and SUMs the spend across all adset rows, using `rows[0]?.currency` for currency.
findings.expected: All rows of one account share the same currency.
findings.actual: If different rows somehow had different currencies (shouldn't happen — single ad account), the sum would mix currencies silently. In practice all rows agree.
findings.fix_sketch: Defensive: validate all rows agree on currency or warn.

findings.failing_input: level=account /insights with `time_range={since:today,until:today}` early in the day (00:00-00:05 IL when there is literally no spend yet).
findings.expected: Returns 0 spend (handled at line 459-462: `if (!row) return { spend: 0, currency: 'ILS' }`).
findings.actual: Correct handling. However, the docstring on line 430 says 'caller (cron-live) wraps in .catch() and degrades gracefully' but the function itself THROWS on non-OK responses (line 451-456). If cron-live does not catch, a transient 500 from Meta will fail the entire live cron run. The contract here is fine; just verify cron-live actually wraps.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a try/catch wrapper version or document the contract more loudly.
findings.regression_test_idea: Test that fetchMetaSpendForDayLight throws on 500 — pinning the contract for cron-live's catch handler.

findings.failing_input: Meta action with action_type = 'omni_purchase' but value = '' (empty string). `parseFloat('') || 0` = `NaN || 0` = 0. Correct.
findings.regression_test_idea: Test action_values entry with empty string value.

findings.failing_input: Both campaign and adset loops soft-fail on per-page errors via `break` after warn(). However, the loop breaks on the FIRST error, even if subsequent pages would succeed.
findings.expected: A transient per-page failure should not orphan later pages.
findings.actual: By design (per MetaAds.gs:218-221 comment). A partial map is preferable to a thrown error, but an intermittent network blip on page 3 of 5 would drop pages 4-5 entirely.
findings.fix_sketch: Implement per-page retry-once before breaking; OR continue with next cursor if available.
findings.regression_test_idea: Test that a mid-pagination 500 stops the loop (pinning current contract).

findings.failing_input: Budget value '999999999999' (~10 billion agorot = 100M ILS). parseFloat handles up to 2^53.
findings.expected: Accurate conversion for any realistic budget.
findings.actual: Correct. Not an issue at any plausible budget level.
